thesis: This episode argues that Google Search represents the single greatest business ever created, generating more profit than any other US company and maximizing value at its IPO. Despite the market currently trading its stock at significantly lower multiples than peers and worrying about AI making its business model obsolete, the thesis maintains that Google's revenue growth remains as fast or faster than most peers, supported by its best-in-time business model and strong data network effects.

claims.claim: Google search is the single greatest business ever created and generates more profit than any other US company.
claims.quote: We tell the story of the single greatest business ever created: Google search. From its origins as a Stanford research project called BackRub, Google became the front door to the internet. Today it’s an essential service for over half the world, and one that generates more profit than ANY other US company — more than Apple, Microsoft, or Berkshire Hathaway.

claims.claim: Google's stock trades at significantly lower multiples than peers despite earning more profits, and investors worry AI will make its business model obsolete.
claims.quote: Today, things are not so obvious once again for Google. Despite earning more profits than all of its big tech peers, its stock trades at significantly lower multiples — a $1 trillion or more discount to Apple, Microsoft and Nvidia. Investors are concerned that AI will render Google’s beautiful business model obsolete, even though Google also basically invented modern AI and continues to lead on ma

claims.claim: Google maximized value at IPO despite initial pricing errors, and its market cap has grown astronomically since.
claims.quote: So you should walk away and say they really maximized value there. They probably were just wrong in that initial range that they were looking for, $108 a share to $135, and it only priced at $85. Well trust the mechanism. I guess it’s only actually worth $85 a share.

claims.claim: Google's market cap is roughly 100x its IPO value, and it has grown to over $2 trillion.
claims.quote: what’s a few percentage points between friends when the company would go to over $2 trillion today as we’re recording this or roughly 100x the market cap when it IPO’d.

claims.claim: Google's revenue growth is as fast or faster than most peers, but the market thinks its future is bleaker.
claims.quote: It’s not like Alphabet’s not growing revenue. They’re growing revenue just as fast, if not faster than all of those companies except NVIDIA. Something is going on here.

claims.claim: Google's business model is the best of all time, supported by a mission to organize the world's information.
claims.quote: It’s not too broad, it’s not too narrow, it feels altruistic, but of course, the business behind it is actually the best business of all time.

claims.claim: Google's data network effects and economies of scale increase revenue as the company gets bigger.
claims.quote: I feel like this is the most unique insight of this episode is whoa, these are economies of scale that don’t just reduce your costs as you get bigger, but it increases your revenue as you get bigger.
